- If sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; apply downward bias correction.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and prices are trending down, model often underestimates; apply upward bias correction.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model frequently overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast slope or add decay factor.
- When sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish mid-period, model often lags in adjusting downward; introduce early warning signal for mean reversion.
- For 30-day forecasts, model exhibits persistent mean reversion bias — if recent 7-day average is above 70, forecast tends to overcorrect; cap forecast at 70.5–71.5 unless sentiment confirms breakout.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to misalign with sentiment direction; align forecast slope with sentiment momentum rather than historical trend.
